Low amber light rakes right across the hive fronts, warming the buttermilk paint to apricot while the grass between the stands stays a deep cool green.
Flat pearl-grey overcast, the light coming evenly from the whole sky, the greens gone deep and saturated under it and the painted timber reading chalky and soft.
A cold pale dawn, every hive roof silvered with dew except one clear dark panel where the colony's own warmth has taken it off, the air a thin washed blue.
Blue-hour dusk with the hive paint gone dusty violet, the orchard behind a solid dark mass, and one warm amber square of shed light falling across the nearest stand.
Hot honey-gold air thick over the stands at mid-afternoon, the clover heads a vivid magenta against it and the painted timber bleached almost white by the direct heat.
Rolling white mist standing to knee height with the hive tops clear above it, the sky above a flat pale cerulean and the box lids beaded wet.
Broken cloud throwing moving patches of bright yellow-green across the meadow, the hive sides swapping between deep teal shadow and full warm cream in seconds.
Fine warm rain falling into cool green shade, the hive roofs dark with wet and the forget-me-nots around the base an intense saturated cobalt.
Steel-blue cloud stacked behind chrome-yellow forage, the rape flowers almost electric against it and the nearest hive side catching a last strip of direct white light.
A deep orange late light stretching long across the apiary, the underside of each hive stand in plain flat shade and the clover tips burning copper.
Silver-green air just after rain, every leaf still beaded, the hive paint a clean saturated turquoise and the sky behind a bruised purple fading to pale grey.
Flat bright noon on painted timber, the colours at full saturation with the red oxide lids sitting hard against a deep sky blue and the grass a sharp lime beneath.
A sudden clear wash after a shower, every colour turned up, the hive sides a clean cobalt blue and the surrounding hedge an almost unreal emerald.
Cold pale pre-dawn with a thin band of rose at the horizon and every hive roof still carrying a grey coat of dew, the air between the stands a soft steel blue.
High-summer afternoon, the air a dense golden amber over the stands and the tall purple loosestrife behind casting cool violet into the lane between hives.
Flat overcast in early spring, the greens punchy and saturated under the white sky, and the hive lids a muted terracotta holding the only warm note in the frame.
A clean high-summer blue sky with the air full of tiny lit specks moving between the hive entrance and the lavender beds, the timber a warm biscuit in full sun.
Thin cloud cover at mid-morning, the light even and cool, the hive sides a deep sage green and the wildflower strip alongside them a vivid scattered orange.
Dawn mist burning off slowly, the low sun a bright tangerine disc behind it, the hive tops emerging clear and the grass still a cold dark teal in the wet.
Blue-hour dusk, the hive paint a washed slate-lavender, a single warm rectangle of amber shed light cutting across the foreground and catching the edge of one super.
Overcast afternoon with the cloud a flat pewter, the blackcurrant bushes behind the hives a saturated dark green and the hive sides a strong sunflower yellow.
Early morning with the air a cool silver-blue, the east-facing hive fronts just beginning to catch a thin apricot warmth and the dew on the roof boards still intact.
Raking amber light at the end of a long summer day, the shadows behind each stand a simple flat cool grey and the entrance boards lit to a deep burnt orange.
A heavy white mist to knee height with the hive boxes clear above, the air above them a cold pale blue and the timber lids dry and warm-toned against the grey below.
Bright and broken mid-morning with fast cloud, the hive sides alternating between a deep cobalt and a warm cream as the light swings through, the grass vivid yellow-green.
